studies.comparison_type: Highest intake versus lowest intake of legumes

studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: The analyses included 82,483 men who completed a detailed quantitative food frequency questionnaire in 1993-1996.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Among men with the highest intake of legumes, the risk reduction was 11% for total prostate cancer (RR = 0.89, 95% CI = 0.80-0.99, p for trend = 0.007) and 26% for nonlocalized or high-grade cancer (RR = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.61-0.90, p for trend = 0.007) compared to men with the lowest intake.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: A total of 4,404 prostate cancer cases including 1,278 nonlocalized or high-grade cases were recorded during the average follow-up period of 8 years.
